Consider the rectangular region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le \sqrt{3},\,\,0\le v\le \frac{\pi }{2}},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v).
$$

Which of the following could be the image of the right side of $Δ$ under the action of $T?$
worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the right side.

For the right side, we have $u=\sqrt{3}$ and $0\le v\le \frac{\pi }{2}.$ 

Substituting $u=\sqrt{3}$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v) \\  & =(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,0\le v\le \frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

This is an equation of a circular arc of radius $\sqrt{3}$ centered at the origin in the $xy$-plane. 
The arc lies in the first quadrant between the polar rays $\theta =0$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14047173/assets/2051bbb1a83dca354f57ff21a1e7208d9acbd9b4122ba8e7406933b449199b52.png)
